name: Old Town and the Mosaic Quarter
tagline: Around St George's Church and the Byzantine map
description: The historic centre holding St George's Church with its sixth-century mosaic map of the Holy Land, the archaeological park with more mosaic floors in situ, and the mosaic school that trains restorers. Stone houses, a tourist street of craft shops, and the whole of it walkable in fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the mosaics and the old town at the door
pros: The Madaba Map and the archaeological park within minutes
Restaurants and craft shops on the tourist street
cons: Tourist pricing on the main street
Coach groups through the middle of the day

name: Madaba Centre
tagline: The working town around the market and the bus station
description: The commercial centre a few streets from the churches, with the produce market, the bakeries, the banks and the shared taxi stand for Amman and the surrounding villages. It is where residents shop and where rents are set for locals rather than visitors, five minutes from the historic quarter.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting local prices with the old town walkable
pros: Market and everyday shopping at local prices
Shared taxis to Amman and the Dead Sea
Five minutes on foot to the mosaics
cons: Ordinary and unremarkable to look at
Few restaurants beyond the local ones

name: Mount Nebo Road
tagline: West towards the viewpoint over the Jordan valley
description: The road running west out of town towards Mount Nebo, where Moses is said to have seen the promised land and where on a clear day you can see Jericho and the towers of Jerusalem. Housing is scattered along the ridge with wide views down to the Dead Sea, quieter and greener than the town.
bestFor: Stays where the view over the Jordan valley is the reason to be there
pros: Views across the valley to the West Bank
Mount Nebo and the Moses Memorial nearby
Quieter and cooler than the town centre
cons: A car or taxi is needed for everything
Ten to fifteen minutes into Madaba
Very few services along the road

name: Hanina and the Northern Suburbs
tagline: The residential expansion, cheapest and newest
description: The newer residential districts spreading north and east of the centre, with apartment blocks, local shops and schools. It is where Madaba's population has grown and where the newest housing stock is, at the lowest rents in town, with the historic quarter a fifteen-minute walk or a short taxi.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a newer flat at the lowest rent
pros: The lowest rents in the town
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes to the old town
No character and nothing to walk to

name: Dead Sea Shore (40 km west)
tagline: Down at the lowest point on earth
description: The resort strip on the Jordanian shore of the Dead Sea, four hundred metres below sea level, reached by a dramatic descent from Madaba's plateau. Hotels, spas and the mud that people come for, plus Hammamat Main hot springs nearby. It is a different climate entirely, hot year-round and extremely dry.
bestFor: Short stays at the sea rather than a base, given the heat and the isolation
pros: The Dead Sea and the hot springs at the door
Spectacular descent road from the plateau
cons: Forty minutes from Madaba and a car is essential
Punishing heat from May to September
Resort pricing and nothing but resorts
